findings.observation: Pre-processed data from Sheet 14 and Sheet 15 blocks.md indicated adjacent properties were labeled with zoning and use information. Vision tool calls confirmed land use labels are present on both sheets 14 and 15. The vision tool identified specific land use designations including 'APARTMENT/CONDO', 'GOVERNMENT SERVICES', 'SINGLE-FAMILY', 'OFFICE', and 'COMMERCIAL' on adjacent property labels.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires a land use map showing adjacent land uses when a site is subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is confirmed subject to Compatibility Standards per Section 10 of the CC Application. The site plan sheets (14 and 15) contain text labels that identify the specific land uses of surrounding properties, not merely zoning designations but actual use descriptions (e.g., 'USE: COMMERCIAL', 'USE: APARTMENT/CONDO'). These sheets function as the land use map and satisfy the requirement.
findings.explanation: Adjacent land uses are labeled on site plan sheets 14 and 15, including single-family, apartment/condo, commercial, office, and government services.

findings.observation: Pre-processed data from Sheet 35 and 36 blocks.md showed building elevations for all four building faces (North, East, South, West) with material legends showing fiber cement board, king brick, wood tone fiber cement, glass, and living wall. Vision tool confirmed Sheet 35 displays architectural elements including facade materials, windows, doors, balconies with railings, and roof lines.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires building elevations showing architectural elements when a site is subject to Compatibility Standards. Sheets 35 and 36 provide comprehensive building elevations for all four building faces. The vision tool confirmed these elevations display architectural elements such as various facade materials, fenestration (windows and doors), balconies, and roof lines. This level of detail satisfies the requirement for building elevations showing architectural elements at the completeness check stage.
findings.explanation: Building elevations on sheets 35 and 36 show architectural elements including facade materials, windows, doors, balconies, and roof lines for all building faces.

findings.observation: Pre-processed data from Sheet 14 blocks.md (Block 4) showed a 'COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINES' table with allowable building heights at different distances from the property line: 0'-10' (no height specified), 10'-25' (0' screening zone), 25'-50' (0' restricted zone), and 50'-75' (40' height limit). Vision tool confirmed compatibility setback lines at 10', 25', 50', and 75' distances are explicitly labeled on the site plan drawing along with the setback table.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning to be shown on plans. The site is adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning to the west, which triggers compatibility standards. Sheet 14 includes both a compatibility setback lines table specifying graduated height restrictions at various distances from the property line and corresponding setback lines drawn and labeled on the site plan itself. This dual presentation (table + graphic depiction) fully satisfies the requirement for showing setbacks adjacent to residential zoning.
findings.explanation: Compatibility setback lines and table are shown on sheet 14, detailing allowable building heights at 10', 25', 50', and 75' distances from the property line adjacent to residential zoning.

summary: All 3 items pass. Site is subject to Compatibility Standards and all required elements are present: land use map showing adjacent land uses (sheets 14-15), building elevations with architectural elements (sheets 35-36), and compatibility setback lines adjacent to residential zoning (sheet 14).
